To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

entropy is not conserved in general, but increases in isolated systems, and that this is the case if and only if entropy is defined as lack of information, and that this definition is the most natural.
the dynamical laws of isolated systems can be formulated by linear transformations which are either unitary or a generalization of Liouville's equation.
entropy is conserved in closed systems if and only if entropy is defined as lack of information, and the dynamical evolution in this case is given by a unitary transformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: (1) The general theory of dynamical transformations and the relation between dynamical transformations and entropy increase.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entropy-increase is an unavoidable consequence of the fact that we do not know the initial state of an isolated system in detail.
entropy increases if and only if there exists an entropy-invariant measure of the state space of the system.
entropy is a measure for lack of information and that the second law follows from this definition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
entropy is a measure of the amount of information needed for the description of a physical system.
the second law of thermodynamics is a consequence of the statistical interpretation of entropy and not of a dynamical law.
the dynamical transformation is a unitary transformation in quantum physics and a generalized form of Liouville's equation in classical physics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamical laws of classical and quantum physics may be unified by a generalized form of the Liouville equation.
the dynamical laws of isolated systems may be derived from a principle of maximum ignorance.
the second law of thermodynamics is a consequence of the interpretation of entropy in terms of information.
